name: HMS Emerald
shortDescription: AP-only British light cruiser, seven fast-reloading 152mm guns backed by a heavy torpedo battery and an unusually full consumable kit.

consumables.name: Damage Control Party
consumables.flavor: 5s action, 60s cooldown, unlimited charges. Same cycle as Omaha's, nothing unique here.

consumables.name: Repair Party
consumables.flavor: +135 hp/s over a 28s duration, about 3,780 hp per charge, 2 charges on an 80s cooldown. A self-heal this early is rare, Omaha carries no Repair Party at all.

consumables.name: Sonar
consumables.flavor: 3.7 km ship detection, 2.7 km torpedo detection, 90s duration, 180s cooldown, 2 charges. Same numbers as Omaha's, useful here for confirming a target before committing AP-only shells.

consumables.name: Smoke Generator
consumables.flavor: 15s lay time, 96s dispersion, 2 charges on a 240s cooldown. Long screen life per charge, but the cooldown means picking one or two moments to use it.

consumables.name: Catapult Fighter
consumables.flavor: 100s uptime, 80s cooldown, 3 charges, one more charge than Omaha gets from the same consumable.

turrets.label: Port Wing
turrets.note: Amidships casemate mount, fixed to port, can't cross to starboard.

turrets.label: Q
turrets.note: Centerline amidships mount, blocked fore and aft by the superstructure, broadside only.

torpedoMounts.label: Starboard 2
torpedoMounts.note: All four mounts fixed to their own broadside, no centerline swing. The Sequential trait lets each mount fire its tubes one at a time instead of a full salvo.

strengths: Improved AP ricochet angles and short fuse timers that are less likely to overpenetrate small targets, so shells arm reliably even against destroyers
4x4 torpedo tubes upgraded, 16 tubes total dealing up to 15,733 damage each, more tubes and more damage per fish than Omaha's torpedoes
Repair Party at tier IV is unusual, Omaha has no self-heal at all
Fast 7s main battery reload keeps all seven guns cycling quickly
A genuinely full consumable kit: heal, sonar, smoke, and fighter cover, not just Damage Control Party
weaknesses: No HE shells at all, AP-only means no fire chance and no reliable way to chip down a heavily angled or bow-tanking target
Thin 10-76mm armor with an exposed citadel, and the Compromising trait means high-caliber AP can still arm through that plating even on an overpenetrating hit
Only seven guns against Omaha's twelve, less raw volume of fire even with the faster reload
6 km torpedo range even fully upgraded, a short leash that forces a real approach to use them
Modest AA (95 DPS total across three short-ranged mounts) with no Defensive AA Fire option, just the Catapult Fighter
tips: Save AP for broadsides or exposed superstructure, there's no HE to fall back on against an angled target.
Lean on Repair Party to shrug off chip damage that would just pile up on a ship without a heal.
Ping with Sonar before committing to a fight, confirming the target matters more when every shell you carry is AP.
Smoke has a long cooldown, save it for a real disengage or a repositioning push rather than routine cover.
Close the range with some caution before a torpedo run, 6 km doesn't give much room for error.

threats.threat: Battleships and heavy cruisers with big-caliber AP
threats.reason: The Compromising trait means their shells can still arm and deal full damage through her thin plating even when they overpenetrate.
No Defensive AA Fire in her kit, just a Catapult Fighter and modest baseline DPS, so plane attacks go mostly unanswered.
10.4 km sea detectability isn't especially stealthy, and her own torpedoes need to close to 6 km to answer back.

summary: AP-only light cruiser, no HE shells at all, built around ricochet-resistant, reliably-arming AP instead
More torpedo tubes than Omaha, 16 upgraded and real damage per hit
One of the few tier IV cruisers with a self-heal, rounded out with sonar, smoke, and an extra-charge fighter
Thin, exposed hull that big-caliber AP can still punish even on an overpenetrating hit
playstyle.detail: Emerald gives up HE entirely and leans all the way into AP, backed by better ricochet angles and fuse timers tuned to arm even against small targets. Seven guns is fewer than Omaha's twelve, but a 7s reload keeps the rate of fire competitive, and the torpedo battery is the real prize, four quad mounts upgraded for sixteen tubes and over 15,000 damage a hit. The consumable kit is unusually complete for the tier: a real Repair Party, Sonar, Smoke Generator, and Catapult Fighter all in the mix. None of that changes the armor, though. She's thin-skinned and the Compromising trait means even overpenetrating hits from bigger guns can still arm and hurt her, so staying unseen and picking the right target matters more than the consumable list might suggest.

Carries Repair Party, Sonar, and Smoke Generator options alongside the standard kit, an unusually full support loadout for the tier.
